question: In the biodiesel produced over GO-Gd2TiO5/g-C3N4, what combined area percentage do the two unsaturated methyl esters (methyl linoleate and methyl oleate) make up?
rendered:
<document title="Engineering a GO-Gd2TiO5/g-C3N4 ternary nanocomposite for enhanced electrochemical performance and biodiesel catalysis">

=== page 14 ===
- Fig. 11 Calibration curve of GO-Gd2TiO5/g-C3N4 modified electrode showing a linear relationship between concentration (0–100 mM) and peak current, with high sensitivity (0.064 mA mM^−1) and low detection limit (0.19 mM).
- The GC-MS chromatogram presented peaks represent-ing four major components labelled with their respective retention times of 16.78, 20.11, 20.90, and 23.26 min.
- Given the GC-MS analysis in Fig. 14(B), it was indicated that methyl stearate was the most abundant FAME of the total chromatogram at 40.59%, followed by methyl oleate at 27.81% and methyl linoleate at 20.51%.
- Finally, methyl palmitate accounted for 9.83% of the total chromatogram.

The combined area percentage of methyl linoleate and methyl oleate is 20.51 + 27.81 = 48.32%.
